parameters.content:
## WF3 — what the second document changed

A document about a product that **already has an approved PRD** is read against that
PRD instead of becoming a new one.

**The delta is computed against the APPROVED version, never the latest draft.** A draft
awaiting review is not what anyone agreed to; deltaing against it would compound
unreviewed output.

**The model proposes and code decides.** `Check the delta` rejects any `req_id` that is
not in the approved version, locates every quote in the new document, and returns the
ledger of what it refused. A delta item is a proposal to change an approved document, so
evidence that cannot be found DROPS the item rather than flagging it.

**Then code writes the version** (E6-S2). A modified requirement keeps its identity in
`origin_req_id`; its `req_id` cannot survive, because ids carry the version and versions are
immutable. Anything the delta does not mention is carried across word for word. A
contradiction is RECORDED and left standing — the PM settles it, not the workflow.

**An empty delta parks and mints nothing.** A version whose changelog is empty is a version
nobody needs to read.
